_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader). Municipal-tier population-priority push, 2026-08-13 (AF/G.18), round 16 of 20 (Wave D). Malawi — 21st-highest-population country, the first of five countries beyond the original top-20 list (skipping Somalia/South Sudan/Burundi, ranked 24/31/30, which already received provincial/national-tier deepening in a prior AF/G.17 session). `mw-nso-cpi` and `mw-sctp-strategic-plan-2022-2027` already cover Malawi's CPI/social-protection tier; this round adds the council fiscal tier. Malawi turns out to have genuinely rich municipal documentation — a live, working named-council-audit pipeline (National Audit Office) and at least one city council (Lilongwe) publishing its own real financial reports.

reports.title: Local Government Act (Cap. 22:01), Malawi
reports.publisher: Government of Malawi / Parliament of Malawi
reports.description: Malawi's organic local government law, verified via the MalawiLII/Laws.Africa consolidated text (as at 2017-12-31). Sec. 79(1): "In every financial year a rate shall be made and levied by the Council to meet some liabilities falling to be discharged out of the general fund," with Sec. 79(4) allowing the council to differentiate rates "between areas and between classes of property." Sec. 44(1): "The sources of revenue for the Council to finance its operations shall be those stated in the Third Schedule." Sec. 64 gives a fallback flat-levy mechanism where formal property assessment is unavailable. Sec. 46(1) establishes a council general fund into which both own-source revenue and central grants flow. Sec. 44(4): "The distribution of Government grants to the Council shall be done by the Government upon the recommendation of the Local Government Finance Committee" — a direct statutory link to the body now operating as the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC).

reports.title: Guidebook on the Local Government System in Malawi
reports.publisher: Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development (MLGRD), Government of Malawi
reports.description: MLGRD's own 2013 guidebook, verified via a ReSAKSS-hosted mirror of the government publication. Establishes the General Resource Fund: "The General Resource Fund (GRF) is the unconditional grant that government transfers to local governments," with a stated usage minimum: "Government however expects local governments to use a minimum of 25% of the GRF for service delivery." Names Malawi's equalization-adjacent mechanism, structurally parallel to Mozambique's FCA/Tanzania's LGFA: "The Local Development Fund (LDF) is a nation-wide financing mechanism for local development that has been established by the Malawi Government to support decentralization." States the closest Malawian analogue to a fixed equalization percentage: "The 1998 Decentralisation Policy goes further by specifying that central government will make available to districts at least 5% of national revenues, excluding grants, to be used for the development of districts." CAVEAT: hosted only via a third-party mirror (resakss.org), not an official malawi.gov.mw domain, though the content is a verbatim Government of Malawi publication.

reports.title: Lilongwe City Council — March 2024 Financial Report
reports.description: Lilongwe City Council's own official site, publishing a genuine financial report with real figures — a positive exception among the four Malawian city councils checked (Blantyre, Mzuzu, and Zomba's own sites were each confirmed to have no equivalent financial documents). "LCC has a total annual budget of MWK16.766 billion. Out of this MWK7.378 billion is under Central Government Transfers (CGT), and MWK9.387 billion under Locally Generated Revenues (LGR)." Revenue performance to date: "A total of MWK 15 billion has been realized in the year representing a 91% performance against the budget revenues." Forward projection: "Total revenue budget for 2024-25 is at MWK29.7 billion."
reports.cadence_note: Periodic council financial report; this is the March 2024 edition. LCC's own site hosts a continuous series back to at least 2021.

reports.title: Report of the Auditor General on the Accounts of the City and District Councils for 2011-2012
reports.publisher: National Audit Office of Malawi (Auditor General)
reports.description: Malawi's National Audit Office reporting on named lower-tier units, verified via direct PDF download — the 'higher tier reporting on named lower-tier units' document type. Individual councils' itemized findings: Lilongwe City Council — "Revenue Not Recorded in the Receipts Cash Book: K136,274,898.73"; "Cash Receipts Not Presented for Audit: K160,933,197.81"; Mangochi District Council — "Revenue Not Accounted For: K15,202,405.05"; Ntcheu District Council — "Payment Vouchers Not Presented for Audit: K22,249,256.78"; Dowa District Council — "Purchases made without IPC authority: K32,743,464.21"; Ntchisi District Council — "Fuel not recorded in the fuel register: K26,033,549.10." NAO's own listing page confirms this report type is published continuously from FY2009-2010 through the year ended 31 March 2025 (14 editions listed), though only the 2011-2012 edition was independently opened and quoted this round — the FY2022-2025 editions remain unverified follow-up leads.
reports.cadence_note: Annual Auditor-General report; this is the 2011-2012 edition, one of a continuous series through FY2024-2025.

reports.title: Final Summary for 2022-23 Council Budget
reports.publisher: National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC), Malawi
reports.description: NLGFC's own consolidated national local-government budget document, verified directly. Constitutional mandate: "Section 149(2) (a)&(d) of the Republican Constitution of Malawi provides mandate to the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) to receive all estimates of revenue and expenditure from all Local Government Authorities and to prepare a consolidated budget." National aggregate: "The 2022/2023 LGA budget is estimated at MK 411.01 billion representing a 31% favorable variance over the approved budget of 2021/2022 financial year which was estimated at K282.52 billion." Locally generated revenue: "has slightly gone up by 23% (27.5 billion) when compared to MK22.31 billion for the 2021-2022 financial year." Structural fact: "City Councils contribute the biggest share (75%) to the Local Revenue Budget." CAVEAT: only accessible via a 'demo.gov.mw' staging mirror of the NLGFC site — the identical path on the canonical www.nlgfc.gov.mw domain returns a 404, and the live NLGFC homepage itself timed out on direct access. Content is genuine NLGFC-authored material, but the hosting-domain instability should be flagged.
reports.cadence_note: Annual consolidated local-government budget summary; this is the FY2022-23 edition.

dependencies.basis: The Auditor-General's audit mandate over council accounts derives from the councils' own statutory general fund (Sec. 46(1) of the Local Government Act) and their statutory obligation to levy and account for rates (Sec. 79) — the audited entities and their revenue categories (rates, receipts cash book, revenue accounting) are the same structures the Act creates, even though this specific report's own text does not quote the Act by section number.

_dropped.edge: Blantyre City Council, Mzuzu City Council, Zomba City Council -> own-published budget/financial-statement documents
_dropped.why: Each site was checked directly. Blantyre City Council's own site (bccmw.com) was reachable but confirmed to have "no links or sections related to budget, finance, financial statements, or annual reports." Mzuzu City Council's own site has a 'Reports' publications subsection but no financial documents were visible/linked. Zomba City Council's own finance-category archive page contains only news-style articles (e.g., IFMIS training, a land-revenue policy statement) and a licence-fee schedule — no budget or financial statement. Lilongwe (mw-lcc-financial-report-2024) is the one clean positive exception among the four.

_dropped.edge: NLGFC's own site (canonical www.nlgfc.gov.mw domain) -> stable primary hosting of mw-nlgfc-council-budget-2022-23
_dropped.why: The canonical www.nlgfc.gov.mw path for this exact document returns a 404, and the live NLGFC homepage itself timed out on direct access; several other nlgfc.gov.mw Joomla k2-component links (e.g. a 'Dissecting sources of revenue for local authorities' article) also 404, consistent with a CMS migration that broke old indexed links. Content was only recoverable via a 'demo.gov.mw' staging mirror. Worth a follow-up check for a stable canonical URL before permanent reliance.

_dropped.edge: Malawi Public Finance Management Act (2003) -> a dedicated General Resource Fund / local-government-transfer section
_dropped.why: Direct full-text review of the PFM Act (consolidated to 2014-12-31) found no dedicated sections on local-government intergovernmental transfers or a definition of the General Resource Fund — the Act applies its Part VIII (Statutory Bodies) to councils only via a general definitional cross-reference to the Local Government Act. The GRF and LDF appear to be administered under Local Government Act / NLGFC-created instruments instead.

_dropped.edge: National Statistical Office of Malawi's own CPI page -> COICOP / IMF-ILO CPI Manual / SADC-COMESA (methodology-prose-level naming)
_dropped.why: NSO's live CPI page (nsomalawi.mw/consumer-price-index) contains only a generic CPI definition, no methodology detail. A separate NSO-authored 'Compendium of Statistical Concepts and Definitions' (April 2023) does formally define COICOP and a 'Harmonised Consumer Price Index (HCPI)' concept in its glossary, but this is glossary-level recognition, not a methodology-chapter statement connecting Malawi's own CPI to COICOP/IMF-ILO Manual/SADC-COMESA — treat as a partial, not full, positive finding, and not yet strong enough to mint a new dependency edge from the existing mw-nso-cpi node.
